paragraphs.text: Brethren, my heart`s desire and my supplication to God is for them, that they may be saved.
paragraphs.original: Ἀδελφοί, ἡ μὲν εὐδοκία τῆς ἐμῆς καρδίας καὶ ἡ δέησις πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν εἰς σωτηρίαν.
paragraphs.translit: Adelphoi, hē men eudokia tēs emēs kardias kai hē deēsis pros ton theon hyper autōn eis sōtērian.

paragraphs.text: For I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.
paragraphs.original: μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτοῖς ὅτι ζῆλον θεοῦ ἔχουσιν· ἀλλʼ οὐ κατʼ ἐπίγνωσιν,
paragraphs.translit: martyrō gar autois hoti zēlon theou echousin· allʼ ou katʼ epignōsin,

paragraphs.text: For being ignorant of God`s righteousness, and seeking to establish their own, they did not subject themselves to the righteousness of God.
paragraphs.original: ἀγνοοῦντες γὰρ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην, καὶ τὴν ἰδίαν ζητοῦντες στῆσαι, τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ὑπετάγησαν·
paragraphs.translit: agnoountes gar tēn tou theou dikaiosynēn, kai tēn idian zētountes stēsai, tē dikaiosynē tou theou ouch hypetagēsan·

paragraphs.text: For Christ is the end of the law unto righteousness to every one that believeth.
paragraphs.original: τέλος γὰρ νόμου Χριστὸς εἰς δικαιοσύνην παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι.
paragraphs.translit: telos gar nomou Christos eis dikaiosynēn panti tō pisteuonti.

paragraphs.text: For Moses writeth that the man that doeth the righteousness which is of the law shall live thereby.
paragraphs.original: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ γράφει ὅτι τὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐκ τοῦ νόμου ὁ ποιήσας ἄνθρωπος ζήσεται ἐν αὐτῇ.
paragraphs.translit: Mōysēs gar graphei hoti tēn dikaiosynēn tēn ek tou nomou ho poiēsas anthrōpos zēsetai en autē.

paragraphs.text: But the righteousness which is of faith saith thus, Say not in thy heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down:)
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ ἐκ πίστεως δικαιοσύνη οὕτως λέγει· Μὴ εἴπῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου· Τίς ἀναβήσεται εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; τοῦτʼ ἔστιν Χριστὸν καταγαγεῖν·
paragraphs.translit: hē de ek pisteōs dikaiosynē houtōs legei· Mē eipēs en tē kardia sou· Tis anabēsetai eis ton ouranon; toutʼ estin Christon katagagein·

paragraphs.text: or, Who shall descend into the abyss? (That is, to bring Christ up from the dead.)
paragraphs.original: ἤ· Τίς καταβήσεται εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον; τοῦτʼ ἔστιν Χριστὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναγαγεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ē· Tis katabēsetai eis tēn abysson; toutʼ estin Christon ek nekrōn anagagein.

paragraphs.text: But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach:
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ τί λέγει; Ἐγγύς σου τὸ ῥῆμά ἐστιν, ἐν τῷ στόματί σου καὶ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τὸ ῥῆμα τῆς πίστεως ὃ κηρύσσομεν.
paragraphs.translit: alla ti legei; Engys sou to rhēma estin, en tō stomati sou kai en tē kardia sou, toutʼ estin to rhēma tēs pisteōs ho kēryssomen.

paragraphs.text: because if thou shalt confess with thy mouth Jesus [as] Lord, and shalt believe in thy heart that God raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved:
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἐὰν ὁμολογήσῃς ἐν τῷ στόματί σου κύριον Ἰησοῦν, καὶ πιστεύσῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου ὅτι ὁ θεὸς αὐτὸν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν, σωθήσῃ·
paragraphs.translit: hoti ean homologēsēs en tō stomati sou kyrion Iēsoun, kai pisteusēs en tē kardia sou hoti ho theos auton ēgeiren ek nekrōn, sōthēsē·

paragraphs.text: for with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.
paragraphs.original: καρδίᾳ γὰρ πιστεύεται εἰς δικαιοσύνην, στόματι δὲ ὁμολογεῖται εἰς σωτηρίαν·
paragraphs.translit: kardia gar pisteuetai eis dikaiosynēn, stomati de homologeitai eis sōtērian·

paragraphs.text: For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be put to shame.
paragraphs.original: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή· Πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: legei gar hē graphē· Pas ho pisteuōn epʼ autō ou kataischynthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek: for the same [Lord] is Lord of all, and is rich unto all that call upon him:
paragraphs.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν διαστολὴ Ἰουδαίου τε καὶ Ἕλληνος, ὁ γὰρ αὐτὸς κύριος πάντων, πλουτῶν εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: ou gar estin diastolē Ioudaiou te kai Hellēnos, ho gar autos kyrios pantōn, ploutōn eis pantas tous epikaloumenous auton·

paragraphs.text: for, Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.
paragraphs.original: Πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου σωθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: Pas gar hos an epikalesētai to onoma kyriou sōthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?
paragraphs.original: Πῶς οὖν ἐπικαλέσωνται εἰς ὃν οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν; πῶς δὲ πιστεύσωσιν οὗ οὐκ ἤκουσαν; πῶς δὲ ἀκούσωσιν χωρὶς κηρύσσοντος;
paragraphs.translit: Pōs oun epikalesōntai eis hon ouk episteusan; pōs de pisteusōsin hou ouk ēkousan; pōs de akousōsin chōris kēryssontos;

paragraphs.text: and how shall they preach, except they be sent? even as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that bring glad tidings of good things!
paragraphs.original: πῶς δὲ κηρύξωσιν ἐὰν μὴ ἀποσταλῶσιν; καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὡς ὡραῖοι οἱ πόδες τῶν εὐαγγελιζομένων τὰ ἀγαθά.
paragraphs.translit: pōs de kēryxōsin ean mē apostalōsin; kathōs gegraptai· Hōs hōraioi hoi podes tōn euangelizomenōn ta agatha.

paragraphs.text: But they did not all hearken to the glad tidings. For Isaiah saith, Lord, who hath believed our report?
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ οὐ πάντες ὑπήκουσαν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ· Ἠσαΐας γὰρ λέγει· Κύριε, τίς ἐπίστευσεν τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: allʼ ou pantes hypēkousan tō euangeliō· Ēsaias gar legei· Kyrie, tis episteusen tē akoē hēmōn;

paragraphs.text: So belief [cometh] of hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.
paragraphs.original: ἄρα ἡ πίστις ἐξ ἀκοῆς, ἡ δὲ ἀκοὴ διὰ ῥήματος Χριστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ara hē pistis ex akoēs, hē de akoē dia rhēmatos Christou.

paragraphs.text: But I say, Did they not hear? Yea, verily, Their sound went out into all the earth, And their words unto the ends of the world.
paragraphs.original: Ἀλλὰ λέγω, μὴ οὐκ ἤκουσαν; μενοῦνγε· Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτῶν, καὶ εἰς τὰ πέρατα τῆς οἰκουμένης τὰ ῥήματα αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Alla legō, mē ouk ēkousan; menounge· Eis pasan tēn gēn exēlthen ho phthongos autōn, kai eis ta perata tēs oikoumenēs ta rhēmata autōn.

paragraphs.text: But I say, Did Israel not know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy with that which is no nation, With a nation void of understanding will I anger you.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ λέγω, μὴ Ἰσραὴλ οὐκ ἔγνω; πρῶτος Μωϋσῆς λέγει· Ἐγὼ παραζηλώσω ὑμᾶς ἐπʼ οὐκ ἔθνει, ἐπʼ ἔθνει ἀσυνέτῳ παροργιῶ ὑμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: alla legō, mē Israēl ouk egnō; prōtos Mōysēs legei· Egō parazēlōsō hymas epʼ ouk ethnei, epʼ ethnei asynetō parorgiō hymas.

paragraphs.text: And Isaiah is very bold, and saith, I was found of them that sought me not; I became manifest unto them that asked not of me.
paragraphs.original: Ἠσαΐας δὲ ἀποτολμᾷ καὶ λέγει· Εὑρέθην ἐν τοῖς ἐμὲ μὴ ζητοῦσιν, ἐμφανὴς ἐγενόμην τοῖς ἐμὲ μὴ ἐπερωτῶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: Ēsaias de apotolma kai legei· Heurethēn en tois eme mē zētousin, emphanēs egenomēn tois eme mē eperōtōsin.

paragraphs.text: But as to Israel he saith, All the day long did I spread out my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.
paragraphs.original: πρὸς δὲ τὸν Ἰσραὴλ λέγει· Ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου πρὸς λαὸν ἀπειθοῦντα καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα.
paragraphs.translit: pros de ton Israēl legei· Holēn tēn hēmeran exepetasa tas cheiras mou pros laon apeithounta kai antilegonta.
